title: Pork Tenderloin with Apples
description: Juicy roasted pork tenderloin with caramelized apples and onions in a quick cider-mustard pan sauce, all in one skillet.

image.alt: Sliced pork tenderloin with roasted apples and onions

steps.text: Heat the oven to {temp 425F oven}. Trim any silvery membrane from the pork and season it all over with the salt, pepper and thyme.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat and brown the pork on all sides, {time 6-8 min} total. Move it to a plate.
Add the butter, apples and onion and cook, turning, until lightly caramelized, {time 4-5 min}. Set the pork on top.
Roast until the thickest part of the pork reads {temp 140F internal}, {time 12-15 min}. Move the pork to a board to rest for {time 5 min}; it will climb to {temp 145F internal}.

Set the skillet over medium heat (the handle is hot). Add the cider, vinegar and mustard and simmer, scraping up the browned bits, until slightly syrupy, {time 3 min}. Slice the pork and serve with the apples and sauce.

notes: Tenderloin is lean, so a thermometer makes all the difference. Slightly pink pork at 145°F is safe and juicy.
